newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian share market ends up on domestic demand.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian share market ends up on domestic demand.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday more than regained Friday's losses, bolstered by the appetite of mostly domestic clients, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 6,327.12 points, up 36.77 or 0.58 percent.
"Mainly domestic investors were buying, foreigners seem to be somewhat more cautious," said Andrea Keresztesi of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Traders said June BUX futures, which traded with negative interest content recently, expired in quiet trade on Monday, ending at 6,337.50 points, down from Friday's settlement price of 6,250.

Hungarian investors were more active despite the fact that on Friday they apparently overreacted to news of a lawsuit against pharmaceuticals Richter Gedeon Rt which had been foreseen in the company's share issue prospectus published in May.
The reaction pushed the share price down 3.5 percent on Friday but the fall was reversed on Monday as Richter ended up 290 at 15,590 forints.
Traders said oil company MOL Rt was the only share which attracted foreign interest, rising 60 to 3,730 forints.
Keresztesi said she was optimistic about the market's outlook for the week and expected higher turnover as foreigners resume interest in the market.
Analysts said as the summer season was approaching the upward momentum may lose some steam before a more promising third quarter.

"(The market) is characterised by some quite high valuations right now," said Tom Chadwick, vice president at Merrill Lynch in London. "As we move towards the summer the upward momentum may slow down somewhat."
Chadwick added he expected some switching into retail stocks and some underperforming stocks "as people start to discount the positive effects of a consumer recovery in 1998."
